'''Charles Akemini Bassey''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Obefelix-Charles Bassey.wav|Listen|help=no}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Charles Akemini Bassey () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/239149-charles-akemini-bassey |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=10 October 2025}}</ref> (born October 28, 2000) is a Nigerian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]]. He was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the second round of [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 53rd overall pick.

==Early life==
Bassey was born in [[Lagos]], Nigeria, where he played [[association football|soccer]] until age 12, standing {{convert|6|ft|1|in|m|2}} at the time.<ref name="courier">{{cite web |last=Estes |first=Gentry |title=How one of the nation's top 2019 prospects, Charles Bassey, ended up playing in Louisville |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/02/14/charles-bassey-2019-basketball-prospect-aspire-academy-louisville/327799002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=February 14, 2018}}</ref> At that age, he was discovered by a youth [[basketball]] coach while Bassey was selling [[fried chicken]] on the side of a road and wearing [[flip-flops]] that were too small for him.<ref name="ujiri">{{cite web |last=Rosser |first=Evan |title=All Access: In Africa with Raptors GM Masai Ujiri |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/big-read-giant-steps-masai-ujiri-giants-of-africa/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=October 11, 2015}}</ref><ref name="lex">{{cite web |title=Charles Bassey: From Selling Fried Chicken In Nigeria At Age 12 To Top Prospect In Four Years |url=http://www.lex18.com/story/34215173/charles-bassey-from-selling-fried-chicken-in-nigeria-at-age-12-to-top-prospect-in-four-years |publisher=[[WLEX-TV|lex18]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=January 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618232811/http://www.lex18.com/story/34215173/charles-bassey-from-selling-fried-chicken-in-nigeria-at-age-12-to-top-prospect-in-four-years |archive-date=June 18, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He stopped playing soccer soon after, instead focusing on developing his basketball skills.<ref name=lex/> At age 14, Bassey was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of basketball camp Giants of Africa, a program established by [[Toronto Raptors]] executive [[Masai Ujiri]].<ref name=ujiri/><ref name="freshman">{{cite web |last=Hickman |first=Jason |title=6-foot-10 Nigerian import Charles Bassey could be high school basketball's best freshman |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/OMSa5fcCQUeU-Z2-xxVbTQ/video-photos--6-foot-10-nigerian-import-charles-bassey-could-be-high-school-basketball%E2%80%99s-best-freshman.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=November 20, 2015}}</ref>

==High school career==
At age 14, Bassey stood {{convert|6|ft|10|in|m|2}} and moved to the United States to continue his basketball career at [[St. Anthony Catholic High School]], a [[private school]] in [[San Antonio|San Antonio, Texas]].<ref name=sporting>{{cite web |last=Hille |first=Bob |title=5-star C Charles Bassey commits to WKU, reclassifies to class of 2018 |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/charles-bassey-western-kentucky-5-star-center-commits-reclassifies-2018/1m66gxyf4cckf1v8jl85tntac4 |publisher=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=June 14, 2018}}</ref> By then, recruiting analysts considered him one of the best prospects in his class.<ref>{{cite web |last=Burlison |first=Frank |title=My Top 35, and more, Pangos Frosh/Soph wrap-up |url=http://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2015/11/charles-bassey-tops-pangos-all-froshsoph-selections/ |publisher=Burlison on Basketball |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=November 12, 2015}}</ref><ref name="express">{{cite web |last=Harvey |first=Buck |title=The next Shaq? Road runs through San Antonio again |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/columnists/buck_harvey/article/The-next-Shaq-Road-runs-through-San-Antonio-again-6603166.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=October 31, 2015}}</ref> As a freshman, Bassey averaged 20.2 points, 17.1 rebounds and 5.9 blocks per game, leading his team to the [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools]] (TAPPS) title game.<ref name="moveover">{{cite web |last=Harris |first=Don |title=Move over Shaq, meet San Antonio's next basketball superstar |url=http://news4sanantonio.com/sports/high-school/move-over-shaq-meet-san-antonios-next-basketball-superstar |publisher=[[WOAI-TV]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=February 26, 2016}}</ref><ref name="ticket">{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=Ticket to the top |url=https://www.expressnews.com/st-anthony-basketball-ticket-to-top/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=June 23, 2017}}</ref> Bassey competed in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game, where he was named MVP.<ref name="jordanbrand">{{cite web |last=Halley |first=Jim |title=Nigerian Charles Bassey makes up for late start, lifts Black team in International game at Jordan Classic |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/charles-bassey-r-j-barrett-montverde-academy-st-anthony-jordan-brand-classic |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=April 15, 2016}}</ref> Before his sophomore season, Bassey was ruled ineligible by the TAPPS, with St. Anthony filing an appeal.<ref name="ineligible">{{cite web |last=Bossi |first=Eric |title=Nation's top sophomore Charles Bassey ruled ineligible |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/nation-s-top-sophomore-charles-bassey-ruled-ineligible |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=November 17, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=St. Anthony names ineligible players, awaits response from TAPPS |url=https://blog.mysanantonio.com/hssports/2016/11/boys-basketball-st-anthony-names-ineligible-players-awaits-response-from-tapps/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=November 18, 2016}}</ref> He still made his season debut, and head coach Jeff Merritt was fired for playing an ineligible player.<ref name="coach">{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=St. Anthony fires coach for playing ineligible Bassey |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/St-Anthony-fires-coach-for-playing-ineligible-10659843.php?t=f40935eb0fbc83a41f |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=December 1, 2016}}</ref> St. Anthony withdrew from the TAPPS and joined the Texas Christian Athletic League, allowing Bassey to become eligible again.<ref>{{cite web |last=Marquez |first=RJ |title=Charles Bassey, other players now eligible as St. Anthony HS leaves TAPPS |url=https://www.ksat.com/sports/charles-bassey-other-ineligible-players-to-return-as-st-anthony-hs-leaves-tapps |publisher=[[KSAT-TV|KSAT]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=December 6, 2016}}</ref>

For his junior season, Bassey transferred to [[DeSales High School (Louisville, Kentucky)|DeSales High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]] and began playing basketball for Aspire Basketball Academy in Louisville. He made the decision after Hennssy Auriantal, his [[legal guardian]] and an assistant coach at St. Anthony, was dismissed from the program.<ref name="auriantal">{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=St. Anthony coach Hennssy Auriantal dismissed after Charles Bassey controversy |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/St-Anthony-coach-Hennssy-Auriantal-dismissed-11342319.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=July 25, 2017}}</ref><ref name="aspire">{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=Boys basketball: Aspire Academy introduces former St. Anthony players |url=https://blog.mysanantonio.com/hssports/2017/08/boys-basketball-aspire-academy-introduces-former-st-anthony-players/ |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=August 26, 2017}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 19.4 points and 12.8 rebounds per game.<ref name="borzello">{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Charles Bassey commits to Western Kentucky, reclassifies to 2018 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23785371 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=June 13, 2018}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Bassey was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top [[center (basketball)|centers]] in the 2018 class. On June 13, 2018, he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2018 class and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers men's basketball|Western Kentucky]].<ref name=borzello/>

==College career==
On November 18, 2018, Bassey recorded a freshman season-high 25 points and 10 rebounds in a 78–62 loss to [[2018–19 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]].<ref>{{cite web |title=UCF beats WKU 78-62 for Myrtle Beach title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401096897 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=November 18, 2018}}</ref> On January 31, 2019, he posted 22 points and 18 rebounds, the most rebounds by a Western Kentucky freshman since 1972.<ref>{{cite web |title=Surging Bassey Wins Sixth C-USA Freshman of the Week Award |url=https://wkusports.com/news/2019/2/4/mens-basketball-surging-bassey-wins-sixth-c-usa-freshman-of-the-week-award.aspx |website=Western Kentucky University Athletics |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=February 4, 2019}}</ref> As a freshman, Bassey averaged 14.6 points, 10 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game, earning First Team All-[[Conference USA]], Defensive Player of the Year and Freshman of the Year honors. He recorded the most rebounds, blocks and [[double-double]]s by a freshman in program history.<ref>{{cite web |last=Stephens |first=Brad |title=Bassey climbing up Hilltopper freshman record lists |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/bassey-climbing-up-hilltopper-freshman-record-lists/article_2fa62486-9c4a-5ef7-999f-f347f6b3a1f5.html |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=January 25, 2019}}</ref> Bassey's sophomore season was cut short by a [[tibial plateau fracture]] he suffered against [[2019–20 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] that required surgery. Through 10 games, he was averaging 15.3 points, 9.2 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Western Kentucky's Charles Bassey out with tibia fracture |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28260966 |access-date=December 10, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 9, 2019}}</ref> 

On November 26, 2020, Bassey recorded 21 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high seven blocks in a 75–69 win over [[2020–21 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]].<ref>{{cite web |last=MacDonald |first=Jared |title=Bassey's Back: Hilltoppers beat Memphis to advance to Crossover Classic final |url=https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/basseys-back-hilltoppers-beat-memphis-to-advance-to-crossover-classic-final/article_fad7a38e-d7ae-55f8-930e-733cf7126d84.html |website=[[The Daily News (Kentucky)|The Daily News]] |access-date=December 2, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> On December 10, he had a career-high 29 points and 14 rebounds in an 86–84 victory over [[2020–21 Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gardner–Webb]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Kim |first=David J. |title=Charles Bassey scores career-high 29 points, helps WKU escape Gardner-Webb with a win |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/12/10/western-kentucky-basketball-charles-bassey-career-high-fuels-win/3849277001/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> At the close of the 2020–21 regular season, he was named the [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]], while repeating as the league's Defensive Player of the Year. He averaged 17.6 points per game, 11.6 rebounds and 3.1 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-mbb-superlative-awards-announced.aspx|title=MBB: Superlative Awards Announced|publisher=[[Conference USA]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}}</ref> Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Western Kentucky center Charles Bassey entering 2021 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31177611 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2021–2022)===
Bassey was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 53rd pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Narducci|title=Sixers second-round pick Charles Bassey willing to show he has a shot|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-nba-draft-second-round-charles-bassey-20210731.html|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=July 31, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}}</ref> subsequently joining them for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers 2021 MGM Resorts NBA Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2021/vegas/team/1610612755/sixers|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 24, 2021}}</ref> On September 24, 2021, he signed with the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Second-Round Pick Charles Bassey|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-charles-bassey|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2021|access-date=September 24, 2021}}</ref>

On October 13, 2022, Bassey was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Pompey|title=Sixers waive Charles Bassey and Isaiah Joe as they work to get roster to 15 players|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-waive-charles-bassey-and-isaiah-joe-20221013.html|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=October 13, 2022|access-date=October 13, 2022}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2022–2025)===
On October 24, 2022, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] announced that they had signed Bassey to a [[two-way contract]], splitting time with the Spurs' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Landon|last=Pederson|title=SPURS SIGN CHARLES BASSEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-charles-bassey-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref> He was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}}</ref> On February 14, 2023, the Spurs converted Bassey's deal to a four-year, $10.2 million standard contract.<ref>{{cite web|first=Cassidy|last=Haffner|title=SPURS CONVERT CONTRACT OF CHARLES BASSEY|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-convert-contract-of-charles-bassey|website=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Dimmitt|title=Spurs Sign Charles Bassey to New Deal: Full Details|url=https://www.si.com/nba/spurs/news/san-antonio-spurs-charles-bassey-sign-contract-gregg-popovich|website=SI.com|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 14, 2023}}</ref> On March 14, during a 132–114 win over the [[Orlando Magic]], he suffered a left knee injury. The next day, the Spurs announced that Bassey was diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture of his left patella, ending his season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Orsborn|title=Charles Bassey's injury puts damper on Spurs' record-setting night|url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/charles-bassey-injury-spurs-record-night-17839934.php|work=San Antonio Express News|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 15, 2023}}</ref> In December 2023, Bassey tore his left [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL), prematurely ending another season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Stiner|title=BREAKING: San Antonio Spurs Player Ruled Out For Remainder Of Season|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/injuries/breaking-san-antonio-spurs-player-ruled-out-for-remainder-of-season-charles-bassey|website=SI.com|date=December 12, 2023|access-date=December 12, 2023}}</ref> On July 8, 2024, Bassey was waived by the Spurs<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Harrison Barnes|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-harrison-barnes|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 8, 2024}}</ref> only to be re-signed nine days later.<ref>{{cite web|author=sasmcasey|title=Spurs Re-Sign Charles Bassey|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-charles-bassey|website=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2024|access-date=July 18, 2024}}</ref>

On July 11, 2025, Bassey played for the [[Boston Celtics]] in the 2025 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Guzman|title=Spurs Free Agent Makes Surprise Appearance at NBA Summer League San Antonio Spurs center Charles Bassey unexpectedly suited up for the Boston Celtics at NBA 2K26 Summer League Friday afternoon|url=https://www.si.com/nba/spurs/news/spurs-free-agent-makes-surprise-appearance-at-nba-summer-league-01jzy25e5pbg|website=SI.com|date=July 11, 2025|access-date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> On September 10, Bassey signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Top NBA Free Agent Centers After Hawks Cut Ties With Charles Bassey|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/top-nba-free-agent-centers-after-hawks-cut-ties-with-charles-bassey-01k7w2vjm1td|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2025)===
On October 26, 2025, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] signed Bassey to a 10-day hardship contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-10-27 |title=Sources: Injured Grizz to add depth with Bassey |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46738767/sources-grizzlies-adding-charles-bassey-via-hardship-exception |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Bassey made two appearances for Memphis, averaging 3.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.0 assist.

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2025–2026)===
On December 27, 2025, Bassey signed with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Acquire Center Charles Bassey From Delaware Blue Coats|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-acquire-center-charles-bassey-from-delaware-blue-coats|website=santacruz.gleague.nba.com|date=December 27, 2025|access-date=December 30, 2025}}</ref>

=== Second stint with Philadelphia 76ers (2026) ===
On January 26, 2026, Bassey signed a 10-day contract with the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=76ers Sign Charles Bassey To 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-charles-bassey-to-10-day-contract |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 5, Bassey signed another 10-day contract with the 76ers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers' Charles Bassey: Receives another 10-day pact|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-charles-bassey-receives-another-10-day-pact/|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> He made one appearance for the team, recording two points and one block. Upon the expiration of his second 10-day deal, Bassey returned to Santa Cruz.

=== Boston Celtics ===
On March 15, 2026, Bassey signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Boston Celtics Sign Center Charles Bassey To A 10-Day Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-boston-celtics-sign-center-charles-bassey-to-a-10-day-contract|date=March 16, 2026|website=GLeague.NBA.com|access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> On March 25, Bassey signed another 10-day contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics Sign Center Charles Bassey To Second 10-Day Contract|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/boston-celtics-sign-center-charles-bassey-to-second-10-day-contract|date=March 26, 2026|website=GLeague.NBA.com|access-date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> In five total appearances for Boston, he averaged 2.8 points and 1.2 rebounds.

=== Golden State Warriors (2026–present) ===
On April 5, 2026, Bassey signed a contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the rest of the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|season]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gordon |first=Sam |date=2026-04-05 |title=Injury-depleted Warriors agree to deal with journeyman Charles Bassey |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/injury-depleted-warriors-expected-sign-journeyman-22190194.php |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wirth |first=Taylor |date=2026-04-05 |title=Warriors sign journeyman center Charles Bassey to an NBA contract amid injuries at position |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/charles-bassey-contract-depth/1928740/ |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=[[NBC Sports Bay Area]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On April 7, he recorded 14 points, 12 rebounds, two steals, and two blocks in a 110–105 victory over the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Takeaways from Warriors' Win Over Kings: TJD Trade Looks Even Better|url=https://www.si.com/nba/warriors/onsi/news/takeaways-from-warriors-win-over-kings-tjd-trade-looks-even-better-01knnh1tpqe0|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

On July 9, 2026, Bassey re-signed with the Warriors on a one–year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warriors Sign Free-Agent Center to Replace Quinten Post|url=https://www.si.com/nba/warriors/onsi/warriors-sign-free-agent-center-to-replace-quinten-post-01kx4bbgnm02|website=si.com|date=July 9, 2026|access-date=July 9, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Shortly after arriving in the United States at age 14, Bassey's mother died. At the time, Bassey considered moving back to [[Nigeria]], but his father Akpan Ebong Bassey encouraged him to stay for financial reasons.<ref name=express/><ref>{{cite web |title=Nike Hoop Summit, World Team notebook: Florida commit Andrew Nembhard is a wizard with the ball |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/hoop-summit/index.ssf/2018/04/nike_hoop_summit_world_team_no.html |publisher=[[OregonLive.com|OregonLive]] |access-date=June 20, 2018 |date=April 11, 2018}}</ref><ref name="custody">{{cite web |last=Zuvanich |first=Adam |title=St. Anthony coach wins custody battle over Bassey |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/article/St-Anthony-coach-wins-custody-battle-over-Bassey-11290027.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=July 14, 2017}}</ref> 

Canadian-born basketball coach, Hennssy Auriantal, who runs the Yes II Success organization that brings international players to American [[private school]]s, helped bring Bassey to the United States.<ref name=courier/><ref name="recruiter">{{cite web |last=Klibanoff |first=Eleanor |title=Louisville's Aspire Academy splits with partner school, controversial recruiter |url=https://wkuherald.com/sports/louisville-s-aspire-academy-splits-with-partner-school-controversial-recruiter/article_cf1f00f0-7629-11e8-a50a-9793d57e308e.html |website=[[College Heights Herald]] |access-date=June 22, 2018 |date=June 22, 2018}}</ref> On March 31, 2017, Auriantal and his wife were granted [[conservatorship]] over Bassey.<ref name=custody/> Bassey's father later filed a petition to reopen the case and give Nigerian basketball tournament organizer John Faniran custody over his son, but the petition was dropped due to lack of verification.<ref name=ticket/><ref name=custody/>
